items.event_time_ist: released Oct 21, 2026 (NYT/Siena University national poll; first carried by Political Wire Oct 21 UTC)
items.title: NYT/Siena national poll: Democrats +11 on the generic congressional ballot
items.summary: New York Times/Siena University national poll finds Democrats leading Republicans 52%-41% on the generic congressional ballot among likely voters. Nate Cohn: 'Eleven is a big number. No party has won the national vote by such a large margin since the Democrats did so in 2008. While the outcome of the midterms will ultimately be decided seat by seat, anything like the results of the poll would probably yield a large Democratic House majority and give the party every opportunity to flip the red states they need to win the Senate, including in states where Democrats simply haven't been competitive in recent years.' Widest top-tier-pollster national-ballot margin of the cycle, two weeks out.
items.source_name: Political Wire (carrying NYT/Siena University pollster release)

items.event_time_ist: Oct 21, 2026 (UNF PORL poll made public Oct 21)
items.title: UNF Florida poll: Donalds 49-47 Jolly ('too close to call'), Moody 49-45 Nixon
items.summary: University of North Florida Public Opinion Research Lab statewide poll of likely midterm voters (MoE +/-2.81, made public Oct 21): governor Byron Donalds (R) 49%, David Jolly (D) 47%; Senate incumbent Ashley Moody (R) 49%, Angie Nixon (D) 45% — both within the margin. Margins narrowed notably from PORL's July poll (Donalds +5, Moody +8); pollster Sean Freeder: 'things really have been tightening in the direction of Democrats doing better.' Contrasts with the Stetson Oct 13 poll (+11 Donalds, already in timeline); DDHQ averages sit at ~Donalds +6, Moody +7. Early voting underway in 35 of 67 FL counties.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 21, 2026 (Marist Michigan Poll released Oct 21; field completed Oct 18 per PollingSource)
items.title: Marist Michigan poll: El-Sayed 50-48 Rogers (Senate), Benson 51-45 James (governor)
items.summary: Marist Michigan Poll (released Oct 21, likely voters, MoE +/-4.3): Senate — Abdul El-Sayed (D) 50%, Mike Rogers (R) 48%, tightening from September (El-Sayed +7 among registered voters then and now); governor — Jocelyn Benson (D) 51%, John James (R) 45% (+11 among RV); Democrats +6 on the Michigan generic congressional ballot among LV (+10 RV). Trump's approval upside down in Michigan; a plurality of likely voters worried about personal finances. PollingSource notes Marist completed Oct 18, 2026.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 20, 2026 (WaPo/ABC News/Ipsos poll findings published Oct 20-21)
items.title: WaPo/ABC News/Ipsos: 70% doubt Trump would accept GOP midterm defeat
items.summary: New Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll findings (published Oct 20-21): 70% of Americans are not confident Trump would accept the results if Republicans lose the midterms — 94% of Democrats, 77% of independents, 36% of Republicans (matches the Dec 2023 reading on the 2024 election). Yet 60% are confident the elections will be conducted fairly (70% Dems, 67% GOP, 51% independents) and 65% are confident votes will be counted accurately — Republican vote-count confidence up from 49% before the 2024 election. 61% are confident Democratic leaders would accept a defeat. Trump told NBC in February he would trust the results 'if the elections are honest.'
items.source_name: Washington Post/ABC News/Ipsos poll (via WaPo reporting)
